name: Hiram
bio:
Hiram (called Huram throughout 2 Chronicles 2) was the king of Tyre who sent messengers to David along with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons, who built David a palace after he was established in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:11) — a gesture of friendship and recognition of David's growing kingdom.

Hiram's alliance with the house of David continued into the next generation. When he heard Solomon had become king, he sent envoys to him, since he had always loved David; Solomon explained that, with his kingdom now at peace, he intended to build the temple the LORD had promised through David, and asked Hiram to supply cedar cut by his Sidonian craftsmen, famed for their skill. Hiram rejoiced to hear it, blessing the LORD for giving David such a wise son, and agreed to supply all the cedar and juniper timber Solomon needed, floating the logs down the coast by sea; in exchange, Solomon supplied Hiram's household with wheat and pure olive oil year after year. The two kings made a formal treaty, and peace prevailed between them as Hiram's materials and Solomon's labor force together built the temple (1 Kings 5).

After twenty years of building the temple and his own palace, having supplied all the cedar, juniper, and gold Solomon desired, Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in Galilee. Hiram went to see them, but they did not please him; he called the region Cabul (meaning something like "worthless") and, apparently in response, still sent Solomon a further 120 talents of gold (1 Kings 9:10-14). Hiram's sailors, experienced with the sea, also joined Solomon's fleet at Ezion Geber, sailing with Solomon's men to Ophir and bringing back 420 talents of gold, along with almug wood and precious stones used to build the temple, the palace, and musical instruments for the singers (1 Kings 9:26-28; 10:11).
